answer: An identity locks 70 credits as bond and files one verified task in each of five distinct sectors of the tundra field. Each filing burns a 30-credit fee and posts one single-key relic receipt to the public knoll ledger, which rejects reused or cross-sector receipts. An auditor recomputes the knoll ledger; a missing tundra sector or duplicate relic burns the bond. 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 credits and burn 150,000 in fees; the k-th fake still owes five fresh filings and 150. A rented portfolio fails on a key mismatch; an honest identity pays 150 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
